title: Working with Files and Folders
text: These questions check that you can read and write files, work with folders and paths, read rest and spread syntax, and work with files safely.

tasks.text: A script calls fs.writeFileSync("report.txt", text) and report.txt already exists. What happens?
choices: The text is added to the end
The file is replaced, without asking
A new file named report (1).txt is made

tasks.text: A script reads fs.readFileSync("members.csv", "utf8"). The file is in the same folder as the script, but Node says it can't find it. What's the most likely cause?
choices: The terminal's current working directory is a different folder

tasks.text: A photo-sorting script moves files with renameSync. Why should it check existsSync first, and what are two other habits that make file scripts safer?
tasks.answer: renameSync silently replaces a file with the same name at the destination, destroying it. Other habits: dry runs; working on a copy; printing process.cwd(); knowing that deletes skip the Recycle Bin.

tasks.text: Why might a photo's modified time (mtime) not be the date it was taken, and what's the alternative?
tasks.answer: mtime is when the file last changed; downloading or copying (e.g. from a chat app or cloud) can reset it. The date taken is stored inside the photo's EXIF data, which needs a package to read.

tasks.text:
Write a function frontMatter(text) that takes the text of a note and returns an object of its front matter: the key: value lines between the first two lines that are exactly ---, splitting each line at the first colon (a value may contain colons). Then write testFrontMatter, which logs JSON.stringify(frontMatter("---
crop: Tomato
note: water at 6:00
---
Planted six seedlings.")).

Make a practice folder with a few text files. Start a new chat with your updated learner profile and ask for a script that renames every .txt file in the folder to start with today's date, like 2027-06-12-notes.txt. (1) Paste the reply. (2) Did it follow the updated rule: a dry run first, and a check before overwriting? (3) Run the dry run, then the real thing on your practice folder, and report the results. (4) What happens if you run it twice? Explain.
tasks.answer: Full credit: rule compliance checked; results reported; running twice would add the date again (e.g. 2027-06-12-2027-06-12-notes.txt) unless the script checks for an existing date prefix. Replies vary, so grade the reasoning.
